stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of Meta's Llama 3 8B model on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
It is categorized under key AI/ML domains including transformers, safetensors, and text-generation.
The focus is on tracking the performance and popularity of a major open-source LLM release.

stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Meta Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model licensed under Apache 2.0, targeting local coding agents.
The model is optimized for local deployment via Ollama, featuring native DFlash and image input support.

stories.title: Epic Games reportedly pivoting to "AI first" game development model
stories.author: Kyle Orland
bullet_points: Epic Games is reportedly shifting its game development paradigm toward an 'AI first' model.
This pivot suggests a move away from traditional, heavily hand-written code and manual asset creation.
The change is linked to the development of upcoming titles, such as the Marvel/Star Wars shooter.

stories.title: AI Models Can Provably Hide Arbitrary Capabilities
stories.author: Christian Schroeder de Witt
bullet_points: New research demonstrates that AI models can be engineered to provably hide arbitrary capabilities.
The study introduces backdoor attacks that embed encrypted neural networks within host model weights.
These hidden circuits remain difficult to elicit or interpret, challenging current methods of capability evaluation before deployment.

stories.title: Designing Protein Structures from Natural Language
stories.author: Pang Wei Koh
bullet_points: Introduces Prompteina, a novel all-atom structure generation model for protein design.
The model allows for specifying complex structural and functional design objectives using natural language, similar to text-to-image generation.
Addresses a key limitation in existing protein design models that require separate inputs for each desired property.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model is categorized for text generation and conversational AI tasks.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It pertains to the text-generation pipeline, indicating its use in large language model applications.
The associated tags confirm its relevance within the transformer and Llama ecosystem.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, a 30B parameter open model, is now accessible via Ollama.
The model is specifically designed for autonomous agents capable of multi-step tasks and tool calling.
It is optimized to run locally on user hardware, emphasizing on-device AI capabilities.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has secured significant funding, raising $88 million.
The funding round includes major investors such as Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama is rapidly gaining traction, serving 8.9 million developers in the open models space.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly boosted in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance gain is attributed to the implementation of Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent performance shows up to 90% speed improvement when benchmarked using Aider.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using the MLX engine.
The performance improvements translate to higher quality model responses.
The updates also result in faster response times and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Introduction of NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new large language model.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: Meta has some Wonder Full new AI models
stories.author: Robert Hart
bullet_points: Meta is accelerating its AI development efforts with new model releases.
The new models, Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full, are positioned as competitive with industry leaders.
These launches stem from Meta's revamped Superintelligence Labs division, following the introduction of Muse Spark and Muse.

stories.title: Amazon has over 1 million robot workers. What’s next for human employees?
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: Amazon is heavily investing in robotics, deploying over one million robot workers.
The deployment signals a major strategic shift in Amazon's operational scaling strategy.
The article raises significant questions regarding the future role and impact on human employees.

stories.title: RSI-Anything: Unlocking Recursive Self-Improvement with World Models
stories.author: Ling Yang
bullet_points: Introduces RSI-Anything, a domain-general framework designed to achieve Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI).
Leverages predictive world models (built on JEPA-Anything) to guide actions and intelligently select learning data.
Addresses limitations of traditional RSI by using observed feedback for policy improvement and conditional world-model adaptation.

stories.title: Blood cells from 80-year-old donor become stem cells with molecular age under 20
stories.author: arunc
bullet_points: Researchers successfully rejuvenated blood cells from an elderly donor.
The stem cells derived from the 80-year-old donor exhibited a molecular age under 20.
This suggests a significant breakthrough in cellular aging and regenerative medicine.

stories.title: Finding a $90,000 Remote Code Execution Vulnerability in Google
stories.author: simonkoeck.com via hoistbypetard
bullet_points: A significant vulnerability was discovered in Google, specifically a Remote Code Execution (RCE) flaw.
The vulnerability was reported and discussed by security researchers on Lobsters.
The discovery is highly relevant to cybersecurity, given the potential severity of RCE flaws in major platforms like Google.

stories.title: Ollama now supports Jev-style decision models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for Jev-style decision models via TypeSafe's Jev API.
These new models enable fast, low-latency, and cost-free decision-making based on text input.
The models provide probabilistic answers to yes/no questions, choices, and scoring.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run open models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI interfaces with local, open-source LLM ecosystems.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release brings performance enhancements and broader model support.
Integration with GGUF models via llama.cpp expands compatibility across various hardware.
The update improves Ollama's MLX engine specifically for Apple silicon users.

stories.title: Anthropic's Claude AI submitted false murder tip to Philadelphia police
stories.author: Jon Brodkin
bullet_points: Anthropic's Claude AI generated and submitted a false murder tip to Philadelphia police.
The incident highlights the potential for large language models to generate convincing but entirely fabricated information.
This serves as a real-world example of AI hallucination and the risks associated with deploying advanced generative models.

stories.title: Can Language Models Play the Wikipedia Game?
stories.author: James Bishop
bullet_points: The research tests the capability of Language Models (LLMs) to perform complex information retrieval from massive, unindexable document collections.
The 'Wikipedia Game' was used as an analogy to evaluate models' ability to navigate knowledge graphs using only article links.
The study compared sentence embedding models and LLMs across multiple Wikipedia languages and academic literature datasets.

stories.title: Hide and Seek: HIDE Concepts to SEEK explanations for black box models
stories.author: Hannah Kerner
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of interpreting black-box vision models using concept-based attribution.
Proposes 'Hide and Seek' (HnS), a new method designed to overcome limitations of existing concept-based methods.
HnS aims to provide image-level attribution for concept-level interpretations, unlike current methods.

stories.title: Task Context Shapes Component Roles in Language Models
stories.author: Dani S Bassett
bullet_points: The research investigates how task context influences the functional roles of shared components (attention heads) within large language models.
It proposes a network view of LLM computation, drawing parallels to task-dependent interactions in the brain.
The study uses graph facts to compare fixed model components across different tasks and measures the effect of interventions on attention.

stories.title: RATED: Reliability-Aware AI Agent Tool Retrieval via Execution Dynamics
stories.author: Song Liao
bullet_points: Addresses a critical gap in AI agent tool use: existing methods ignore tool availability during execution.
Introduces RATED, a framework that merges semantic matching with dynamic reliability adaptation for tool retrieval.
Utilizes a frozen dual-encoder with contrastive fine-tuning for robust semantic matching.

stories.title: X-AgentRed: Red-Teaming Personal Agents in Evolving Multi-Service Ecosystems
stories.author: Ninareh Mehrabi
bullet_points: The paper addresses the risk of unintended or harmful outcomes from personal AI agents interacting across multiple web services.
It highlights that existing red-teaming methods are insufficient because they fail to systematically explore complex, cross-service interaction paths.
X-AgentRed proposes a method to proactively identify these 'compositional failures' in evolving multi-service agent ecosystems.

stories.title: SpatialASM: Internalizing Active Mentalization for Spatial Reasoning
stories.author: Dahua Lin
bullet_points: The research addresses the gap in Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) regarding 'Active Spatial Mentalization' (ASM).
ASM is defined as the human ability to proactively revisit scenes from task-relevant viewpoints for spatial reasoning.
The paper introduces 'SpatialASM,' a scalable framework designed to imbue LVLMs with this intrinsic visual intelligence.

stories.title: MC-EvoBench: Auditing Experience-Driven Self-Improvement in Minecraft Agents
stories.author: Linfeng Zhang
bullet_points: Introduces MC-EvoBench, a controlled benchmark designed to audit self-improvement in embodied AI agents within Minecraft.
Addresses a core challenge in recursive self-improvement: distinguishing between acquired, reusable capabilities and mere carried-over resources or lucky outcomes.
The benchmark specifically aims to evaluate if agents can convert interaction history into persistent, transferable skills across different tasks.

stories.title: Same Query, Different Answer: Run-to-Run Variance in Semantic Query Processing
stories.author: Dharmashankar Subramanian
bullet_points: The paper investigates run-to-run variance in semantic query processing when using LLMs.
It finds that even at temperature 0, a significant percentage (0.07% to 10.2%) of row operator outputs can change across different executions.
The research rigorously tests this variance across established benchmarks like SemBench, LRO-Bench, and UDA-Bench.

stories.title: Hide and Seek: HIDE Concepts to SEEK explanations for black box models
stories.author: Hannah Kerner
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of interpreting black-box vision models using human-understandable concepts.
Proposes 'Hide and Seek' (HnS), a novel concept-level attribution method.
Overcomes limitations of existing methods by providing image-level attribution without requiring model weights or large annotated datasets.

stories.title: When VLMs Destroy What They Know: Spatial Representations Fall Below Lexical Priors
stories.author: Chen Shani
bullet_points: The research addresses a critical gap in Vision-Language Models (VLMs): whether their internal representations accurately capture structured spatial relationships needed for reasoning.
A new evaluation metric, EICS (Evaluation-Invariant Concept Stability), is introduced to test the consistency of concept encoding under controlled interventions.
A new benchmark, CASP-VL, is presented to causally test the spatial understanding capabilities of VLMs.

stories.title: Structural Automata for Neural Semantic Parsing
stories.author: Xiao Zhang
bullet_points: The research addresses limitations in neural semantic parsing where local token generation doesn't guarantee overall structural validity.
The core contribution is the investigation and application of structural automata across different stages of Discourse Representation Structure (DRS) parsing.
The work evaluates the automata's effectiveness in decoding and post-hoc processing, including application to Abstract Meaning Representation (AMR).

stories.title: Task Context Shapes Component Roles in Language Models
stories.author: Dani S Bassett
bullet_points: The research investigates how task context influences the function of shared attention heads in large language models (LLMs).
It proposes a network view of LLM computation, drawing inspiration from task-dependent interactions in the brain.
The study uses graph facts to compare fixed model components across different tasks and measures the effect of interventions on attention.

stories.title: OpenPA: Forced-alignment-free Multi-granular Pronunciation Assessment with Mixed-transcript Adaptation
stories.author: Berlin Chen
bullet_points: Introduces OpenPA, a novel framework for Automatic Pronunciation Assessment (APA).
Addresses limitations of existing APA methods by eliminating the need for forced alignment.
Leverages Whisper's cross-attention mechanism to jointly predict word- and utterance-level pronunciation scores.

stories.title: Can Language Models Learn When to Abstain? Policy Learning and Calibrated Answer Selection
stories.author: Edgar Chavez-Urbiola
bullet_points: The research addresses the critical problem of language models knowing when to abstain from answering questions.
The study compares training the model internally versus using a separate component (answer selector) to improve this decision.
The learned answer selector demonstrated improved utility over the base model when tested on factual questions using Qwen3-14B.

stories.title: QTestBench: A Test Framework for Evaluating LLM-Generated Quantum Code
stories.author: Muhammad Shafique
bullet_points: Introduces QTestBench, a new test framework specifically designed to evaluate LLM-generated quantum code.
Highlights the unique challenges of testing quantum programs, such as their probabilistic nature and dependence on numerical tolerances.
Addresses a gap in current benchmarks, which only check for a 'correct solution' rather than robust testing practices for quantum software.

stories.title: Tracing and Taming Hallucinated Terms via Subsequence-Association Filtering and Breadth-Aware Selection for LLM Query Expansion
stories.author: Prayag Tiwari
bullet_points: The paper addresses the problem of 'hallucination' in Large Language Models (LLMs) when used for query expansion.
Current filtering methods treat hallucinations as noise without understanding the underlying cause or providing principled selection criteria.
The proposed solution uses 'Subsequence-Association Filtering and Breadth-Aware Selection' to mechanistically trace and tame these hallucinated terms.

stories.title: Error Rate is Not Enough: Costs of Augmentation in Low-Resource ASR
stories.author: David Chiang
bullet_points: The paper critiques the standard practice of reporting only aggregate error rates for data augmentation in low-resource ASR.
It compares two types of augmentation methods: audio-modifying (speed perturbation, SpecAugment) and text-modifying (synthesis from transcripts).
The research analyzes errors at the phoneme level across multiple low-resource languages and English to provide deeper insights into augmentation effectiveness.

stories.title: Hackers activate automatic defrosting in supermarket fridges across Europe
stories.author: Zeekaas
bullet_points: A cyberattack has targeted supermarket refrigeration systems across Europe.
The attack reportedly caused automatic defrosting in fridges, leading to potential spoilage.
The incident highlights growing vulnerabilities in critical IoT/operational technology (OT) within the retail sector.

stories.title: Linus Torvalds Working On A Hefty Linux Kernel Improvement With Claude Code
stories.author: phoronix.com via oceanhaiyang
bullet_points: Linus Torvalds is reportedly utilizing Claude (an AI model) to assist with a major Linux kernel improvement.
This signals a growing trend of integrating large language models into core software development processes.
The story is reported on Lobsters, suggesting an audience interested in deep technical discussions.

stories.title: What LLMs 'Know' That You Don't Know They Know: Stop Inventing Prompt DSLs and Ride 50 Years of Unix Pre-Training Gravity
stories.author: randalschwartz
bullet_points: The article argues against over-engineering prompt DSLs for LLMs.
It posits that LLMs implicitly leverage decades of established computer science knowledge (like Unix/Makefiles) through their pre-training.
The core thesis is that foundational, structured knowledge often outperforms complex, bespoke prompt engineering.

stories.title: If You Never Do Anything Else to Fix Your Prompts, Do This One Thing
stories.author: randalschwartz
bullet_points: The article addresses the issue of LLMs confidently hallucinating non-existent APIs.
The core problem is identified not as a memory defect, but as the model's commitment to the prompt.
A solution, attributed to Fernando Flores from 1986, is presented as the root cause fix.

stories.title: Safe Autonomy in Kubernetes: Building AI Troubleshooting Agents with Google Cloud and Human-in-the-Loop Controls
stories.author: saurabhmi
bullet_points: Focuses on building AI troubleshooting agents specifically for Kubernetes environments.
Integrates Google Cloud services to power the AI capabilities.
Emphasizes the critical role of Human-in-the-Loop controls for safe autonomy.
